dominant_strengths: Confident headline typography paired with warm peach product mockup creates clear focal hierarchy and brand warmth
Product screenshot demonstrates the value proposition immediately, combining desktop and mobile views with realistic task data
Restrained palette of cream, coral, and neutral grays feels coherent and on-brand for Todoist
dominant_weaknesses: Cookie consent modal collides with the close button and crowds the lower-right, breaking the otherwise calm composition
Left column feels under-supported: the reviews badge with star glyphs looks dated and visually fights the clean headline
Hero is generic SaaS layout — no distinctive system or motion cue to differentiate beyond the product screenshot itself
fix_priorities: Fix the consent modal layering and close-button collision; restyle as a compact, non-intrusive bar
Redesign the social-proof badge with proper star icons and clearer typographic rhythm
Introduce a subtle interaction or animation in the hero mockup to elevate motion elegance
Add a more distinctive visual signature (illustrative accent, typographic detail) to escape template feel
rationale.norman_balance: Behaviorally clear and reflectively trustworthy via product proof, but visceral impact is muted by a conventional hero pattern.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — it communicates Todoist's clarity-and-simplicity promise effectively, though it under-delivers on distinctiveness for a category-defining product.
